title: Fleet stability stitch-up: weekly operational synthesis (Nov 14 2028)
content:
Weekly synthesis (Nov 14 2028) - Fleet stability stitch-up

Attendees: Maya Patel (owner), Jordan Kim, Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Ethan Brooks, oncall rotation: team-infra-a

Summary
- This note stitches together operational signals from the week and surfaces prioritized actions. Overall fleet is stable but a pattern of short regional slot shadows in eu-west and apac-sg is causing intermittent latency spikes for Dedicated customers.
- We ran two experiments this sprint: a conservative prewarm (prewarm-v2) and a drain-aware scheduling tweak (slot-shadow-mitigation). Prewarm-v2 reduced cold-start tail by ~28% for 2k-4k token requests.

Key metrics (last 7 days)
- Average GPU utilization (fleet-wide): 67% (target 65-75)
- Regional available slots (normalized): us-west 14%, eu-west 9%, apac-sg 6%
- Cold-start tail (95p token latency): baseline 540ms -> prewarm-v2 390ms
- Prewarm hit rate (requests benefiting from warm KV-cache): 42% fleet, eu-west 34%
- Autoscaler churn events (scale up/down oscillations): 18 events (goal <10)
- SLO breaches (p50/p95) for hosted API: 0.3%/1.8% respectively

Incidents & near-misses
- 2028-11-11 02:16 UTC (eu-west): 15m slot shadowing caused by coordinator leader bounce during k8s node maintenance. Impact: Dedicated contours experienced degraded throughput for 23 customers. Mitigations applied: emergency failover to us-west and temporary increase of soft-capacity limits. Postmortem in JIRA-OPS-2147.
- 2028-11-12 19:40 UTC (apac-sg): preemptible node eviction + delayed autoscaler reaction produced a shortfall of 120 slots. Root cause: autoscaler cooldown logic didn't account for batched drain annotations. Fix being rolled: PR #482 (drain-aware cooldown).

Capacity planning (next 2 weeks)
- Short term (0-3 days): Increase eu-west spare buffer from 9% -> 15% via reserve-pack add of +12 gpus to handle seasonal marketing spikes for customer X (ticket: JIRA-PRIME-3091).
- Mid term (3-14 days): Move forward with staggered regional purchases for apac-sg to reach 12% spare buffer; target provisioning date: 2028-11-25.
- Note on hedging: prefer capacity in apac-sg over apac-tok due to lower preemption rates observed in last 60 days.

Playbook updates (recommended)
- Introduce "slot-shadow-detection" entry to the oncall runbook: automated alert when regional available slots drop >30% within 10m and autoscaler churn >5 events in 1h. Triage steps: (1) check coordinator leader health, (2) probe node drain annotations, (3) trigger emergency reserve pack request.
- Add prewarm-v2 as the default on smaller GPU flavors for model types A/B (where median seq_len < 2k).

Experiments & learnings
- Prewarm-v2: uses staggered KV warming with a small LRU bias toward recent tenants. Result: improved 95p latency and reduced token-level cost for short bursts. Tradeoffs: increases steady-state memory pressure by ~4% on node. Action: instrument a per-node prewarm pressure metric and cap prewarm concurrency to 12 per GPU.
- Slot-shadow-mitigation: the scheduling tweak reduced observed slot shadows during controlled drain tests by 60%. Unexpected: interaction with bin-packing heuristic increased fragmentation for low-memory models. Follow-up: tweak bin-packer threshold and rerun sim.

Action items (owner - due)
- Maya: submit procurement change request for eu-west reserve-pack (+12 GPUs) and track contract approval. (due 2028-11-16)
- Jordan: finish drain-aware cooldown rollout and monitor autoscaler churn metric; follow up on PR #482. (due 2028-11-15)
- Priya: add slot-shadow detection rules to PagerDuty and update runbook snippet. (due 2028-11-17)
- Liam: add prewarm pressure telemetry to node exporter and dashboard. (due 2028-11-18)
- Ethan: run bin-packer fragmentation sim with new thresholds and capture cost delta. (due 2028-11-20)

Notes and discussion points
- Is there appetite to accept a small memory pressure increase for a large reduction in cold-start latency for mid-tier customers? Suggestion: rollback knob per-customer tier.
- We should coordinate eu-west reserve-pack procurement with Finance (cost planning session on 2028-11-16).
- Consider a brief "regional priming window" aligned to marketing pushes; ops will pro-emptively bump prewarm concurrency for expected spikes. Need checklist and owner.

Attachments & links
- Postmortem: JIRA-OPS-2147
- Autoscaler fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-monitoring/pull/482
- Procurement ticket: JIRA-PRIME-3091

Appendix: quick runbook snippet (copyable)
- Alert: slot-shadow-detection -> runbook steps:
  1) Check leader from /proc/fleet/leader-status
  2) kubectl get nodes -l drain=true -o wide
  3) If leader bounce detected: escalate to platform-ops and trigger emergency region failover play (runbook id: region-failover-v3)
  4) If autoscaler cooldown: flip cooldown to short-window (30s) for emergency window and annotate incident.

Next meeting: Weekly ops sync (Mon 2028-11-20 16:00 UTC). Focus: eu-west packetization, apac provisioning cadence.

End of note.
